chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, who reported from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Zurarah ibn A'yan who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali (peace be upon them) told me:

"O Zurarah, beware of the people who apply analogy in the matters of religion. For indeed they have abandoned the knowledge of what was entrusted to them and have burdened themselves with what had already been decided for them. They misinterpret the traditions and fabricate lies against God, Mighty and Majestic. And as if I see a man among them who, when called from the front, answers from behind, and when called from behind, answers from the front. They have become lost and bewildered on the earth and in religion."

key_terms.الأخبار: Al-Akhbar (traditions/reports) - narrated sayings of the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.القياس: Qiyas (analogy) - a method of legal reasoning by drawing parallels from existing rulings to new cases, rejected in Shia jurisprudence as a source of law
key_terms.تاهوا: Tahu - to become lost, wander aimlessly, deviate from the right path

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about qiyas (analogy) in religion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) warns his prominent companion Zurarah ibn A'yan against those who apply qiyas (analogical reasoning) in religion. In early Shia jurisprudence, this was a major methodological dispute between the Ahl al-Bayt school and certain Sunni jurists who favored qiyas. The Imam condemns them for abandoning the transmitted knowledge of the Imams in favor of their own flawed reasoning, resulting in confusion and falsehood.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 12. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Waleed, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, who reported from Ya’qoob ibn Yazeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Zurarah ibn A’ayan who said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him, told me:

"O Zurarah, keep away from the people who apply analogy in the matters of religion. Surely, they have abandoned the knowledge of what was assigned to them, and entered into unnecessary hair splitting matters, which had already been decided for them. They interpret the Traditions (the way they like) and impute lies to Allah, Most High. And as if I see a man among them who when called from the front, answers to the one behind him, and when called from behind, he hearkens to the one in front. They wonder aimlessly on the earth and in religion."
